parsed.answer: Gross margin is not a meaningful metric for American Express. As a financial services/payments company, American Express does not report a "cost of goods sold" and thus has no gross margin line item; its business model is built on net interest income and non-interest revenues (discount revenue, fees, etc.) offset by provisions for credit losses and operating expenses (rewards, marketing, salaries, etc.), rather than a manufacturing/retail cost structure where revenue minus cost of goods sold produces a gross margin. A more relevant profitability driver for FY2022 is the movement in total revenues net of interest expense after provisions for credit losses, and pretax/net income. For FY2022, total revenues net of interest expense after provisions for credit losses rose to $50,680 million from $43,799 million in 2021, driven by growth in discount revenue ($30,739 million vs. $24,563 million) and net interest income ($9,895 million vs. $7,750 million), as well as higher provisions for credit losses ($2,182 million vs. a benefit of $(1,419) million in 2021). However, total expenses also increased substantially (from $33,110 million to $41,095 million), driven by higher Card Member rewards, business development, marketing, and salaries and employee benefits, which caused pretax income to decline to $9,585 million from $10,689 million, and net income to fall to $7,514 million from $8,060 million.
